```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE)
data("hfi", package = "openintro")
num <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 3, format = "f")
scatter <- function(model, labels, title) {
  d <- model.frame(model)
  plot(d[[2]], d[[1]], xlab = labels[1], ylab = labels[2],
       main = title, pch = 16, cex = 0.55)
  abline(model, lwd = 2)
}
diagnostics <- function(model) {
  e <- residuals(model)
  fit <- fitted(model)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
  plot(fit, e, xlab = "Fitted value", ylab = "Residual", pch = 16, cex = 0.45)
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
  lines(lowess(fit, e), lwd = 2)
  hist(e, breaks = 25, xlab = "Residual", main = "Residual histogram")
  qqnorm(e, pch = 16, cex = 0.45)
  qqline(e, lwd = 2)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}
d1 <- hfi[complete.cases(hfi[, c("pf_expression_control", "pf_score")]), ]
m1 <- lm(pf_score ~ pf_expression_control, data = d1)
```

## 1. Dataset dimensions

```{r}
dim(hfi)
```

The dataset has `r nrow(hfi)` country-year observations and `r ncol(hfi)` variables.

## 2–3. Media freedom and personal freedom

```{r}
scatter(m1, c("Political pressure and controls on media (higher = less pressure)",
              "Personal freedom score"),
        "Personal freedom by media freedom score")
r <- with(d1, cor(pf_expression_control, pf_score))
r
outliers <- order(abs(rstandard(m1)), decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]
cbind(d1[outliers, c("countries", "year", "pf_expression_control", "pf_score")],
      residual = residuals(m1)[outliers])
```

**2.** A scatterplot shows the relationship between these two numerical
variables. The overall pattern is approximately linear and increasing.
A line is reasonable for a rough prediction within the observed range.
There is enough scatter that a prediction for one country-year can still
be noticeably off.

**3.** The correlation is `r num(r)`, indicating a strong positive association.
The table identifies three unusual observations with the largest absolute
standardized residuals. These country-years lie farther from the line than
most observations.

## 4. Minimizing the sum of squared residuals

Run the following in an interactive R session to compare lines selected by hand.

```{r eval=FALSE}
DATA606::plot_ss(x = d1$pf_expression_control, y = d1$pf_score, showSquares = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Reproduce the line comparison without clicking on a plot.
x <- d1$pf_expression_control
y <- d1$pf_score
candidate_slopes <- c(0.35, 0.45, 0.50, 0.60)
candidate_intercepts <- mean(y) - candidate_slopes * mean(x)
trial_ss <- mapply(function(a, b) sum((y - (a + b * x))^2),
                  candidate_intercepts, candidate_slopes)
data.frame(intercept = candidate_intercepts, slope = candidate_slopes,
           sum_of_squares = trial_ss)
c(exact_least_squares = sum(residuals(m1)^2))
```

The best candidate line has a residual sum of squares of
`r num(min(trial_ss))`. The exact least-squares solution reaches
`r num(sum(residuals(m1)^2))`. A hand-picked line using
`DATA606::plot_ss()` can be compared with this minimum using the same rows.

## 5. Predicting overall human freedom

```{r}
m2 <- lm(hf_score ~ pf_expression_control, data = hfi)
coef(m2)
```

The fitted overall human freedom score is
`r num(coef(m2)[1])` + `r num(coef(m2)[2])` times the media-control score.
Each one-point rise in the media-control score, which indicates less
political pressure, is associated with a fitted increase of
`r num(coef(m2)[2])` points in overall human freedom. The association
does not establish causation.

## 6. Prediction and residual at 6.7

```{r}
prediction <- unname(predict(m1, newdata = data.frame(pf_expression_control = 6.7)))
matches <- abs(d1$pf_expression_control - 6.7) < 1e-8
match_type <- "Exact recorded 6.7"
if (!any(matches)) {
  matches <- round(d1$pf_expression_control, 1) == 6.7
  match_type <- "Recorded predictor rounds to 6.7"
}
matching <- d1[matches, c("countries", "year", "pf_expression_control", "pf_score")]
matching$predicted_at_6.7 <- rep(prediction, nrow(matching))
matching$observed_minus_prediction <- matching$pf_score - matching$predicted_at_6.7
matching$direction <- ifelse(matching$observed_minus_prediction > 0, "underestimate",
                             ifelse(matching$observed_minus_prediction < 0,
                                    "overestimate", "exact"))
match_type
matching
```

The regression predicts **`r num(prediction)`** for a media score of 6.7.
The residual is observed personal freedom minus the prediction. A positive
number means an underestimate, and a negative number means an overestimate.
The table gives the answer for each matching country-year. When a recorded
value was rounded to 6.7, the displayed difference uses the requested 6.7.

## 7–9. Model diagnostics

```{r fig.width=11, fig.height=4}
diagnostics(m1)
```

```{r}
e <- residuals(m1)
fit <- fitted(m1)
smoother <- lowess(fit, e)
quartile <- cut(fit, breaks = unique(quantile(fit, seq(0, 1, 0.25))),
                include.lowest = TRUE)
spread <- tapply(e, quartile, sd)
skew <- mean((e - mean(e))^3) / mean((e - mean(e))^2)^(3 / 2)
c(residual_sd = sd(e), max_abs_smoothed_residual = max(abs(smoother$y)),
  residual_skewness = skew)
spread
```

**7.** The overall trend can be approximated by a line, but the residual
smooth bends. The straight line leaves some systematic structure, so
linearity is approximate.

**8.** The histogram and Q–Q plot show departures from normality, especially
in the tails. The residual skewness is `r num(skew)`. A normal error model
is an approximation, especially for predicting an individual country-year.

**9.** The vertical spread changes across fitted values. The residual standard
deviations by fitted quartile range from `r num(min(spread))` to
`r num(max(spread))`, so constant variability is questionable. Repeated
country-years also mean standard regression inference may require accounting
for dependence within countries.

## More practice

```{r}
comparison <- hfi[complete.cases(hfi[, c("pf_score", "pf_expression_control",
                                        "pf_religion")]), ]
media_model <- lm(pf_score ~ pf_expression_control, data = comparison)
religion_model <- lm(pf_score ~ pf_religion, data = comparison)
scatter(religion_model, c("Religious freedom score", "Personal freedom score"),
        "Personal freedom by religious freedom")
r2_media <- summary(media_model)$r.squared
r2_religion <- summary(religion_model)$r.squared
c(media_control = r2_media, religious_freedom = r2_religion)
```

**1.** Religious freedom and personal freedom show a positive relationship
that a straight line can summarize, although the scores are bounded and
there is scatter at a given religious freedom score.

**2.** On the same complete country-years, the religious freedom model has
R-squared `r num(r2_religion)` and the media model has R-squared
`r num(r2_media)`. The
`r if (r2_media >= r2_religion) "media control" else "religious freedom"`
score explains at least as much in-sample variation in personal freedom in
this comparison. Both predictors describe components of the broader personal
freedom index, so part of the relationship reflects how the index is built.

**3.** I was interested in how strongly personal freedom tracks economic
freedom. The two measure different aspects of society, yet can move
together because they share country-level influences.

```{r fig.width=11, fig.height=4}
economic_model <- lm(pf_score ~ ef_score, data = hfi)
summary(economic_model)
diagnostics(economic_model)
```

The residual and Q–Q plots show where the line and normal-error approximation
fit poorly. The fitted association summarizes the data and does not measure
how a policy change would affect personal freedom.
